# Vulkan, retained composition, and software rendering

## Renderer selection

`WindowOptions.renderer` accepts:

- `RendererPreference.automatic` — try Vulkan, preserve the failure reason, then use software;
- `RendererPreference.vulkan` — require Vulkan and throw on failure;
- `RendererPreference.software` — never initialize Vulkan.

`AURORA_RENDERER=vulkan|software` overrides the option for diagnostics and deployment.

```d
WindowOptions options;
options.renderer = RendererPreference.automatic;
options.vsync = true;
options.lowLatency = true;
auto window = new GuiWindow(options);
```

## What the GPU renders

Aurora's Vulkan path receives indexed geometry, not a completed CPU framebuffer. Rectangles, lines, circles, rounded rectangles, gradients, icons, and glyph quads are rasterized by the GPU. The CPU performs widget layout, Unicode/OpenType text layout, primitive tessellation, and one-time glyph-outline rasterization only when the corresponding content is dirty.

Version 0.4.2 adds a retained scene above the renderer:

```text
base DrawList (revision B)
retained layer 1 DrawList (revision A) + device bounds
retained layer 2 DrawList (revision C) + device bounds
                         │
                         ▼
                    RenderScene
```

A layer's draw list is local to that layer. Moving it changes `deviceBounds.x/y` without changing the draw list revision.

## Retained Vulkan geometry

The Vulkan renderer keeps one `GpuLayerGeometry` entry per scene-layer ID. Each entry owns persistent mapped vertex/index buffers plus the content revision, local viewport, atlas dimensions, and index count used to create them.

Geometry is uploaded only when one of these changes:

- layer content revision;
- layer width or height;
- glyph-atlas dimensions.

During a transform-only frame Aurora:

1. selects an idle frame context without waiting;
2. acquires a swapchain image with timeout zero;
3. late-latches the current captured pointer and refreshes only layer origins;
4. verifies that base and layer revisions are unchanged;
5. records a dynamic viewport for each layer's current device bounds;
6. translates local clips into framebuffer scissors;
7. binds the already-retained buffers;
8. draws and presents.

No widget layout, text shaping, tessellation, or geometry upload occurs for a position-only drag. See [Retained compositor](RETAINED_COMPOSITOR.md).

## Pipeline

Aurora uses one graphics pipeline:

- triangle-list input;
- position, atlas UV, and RGBA vertex attributes;
- one combined image sampler for the shared R8 glyph atlas;
- nearest filtering and clamp-to-edge for 1:1 A8 coverage;
- straight-alpha source-over blending;
- dynamic viewport and scissor;
- no depth or stencil attachment;
- one color swapchain attachment.

Solid geometry samples a permanent white atlas texel, so shapes and text share the pipeline and descriptor set.

Painter order remains base first and then retained layers in widget z-order. Aurora does not reorder translucent geometry or layers.

## Logical and physical coordinates

Widget layout and input use 96-DPI logical units. Each `DrawList` records both `logicalViewport` and physical `viewport`, plus `DisplayScale`. Primitive edges and clips are converted to framebuffer pixels while recording. Text layout remains logical, but glyph outlines are rasterized at monitor-scaled pixel size and their quads are snapped to physical pixels.

Retained-layer positions are converted from logical global bounds to physical `deviceBounds`. The layer's local geometry remains independent of its position. See [High-DPI rendering](HIGH_DPI.md).

## Glyph atlas

All draw lists in one `GuiWindow` share the window's `FontSystem` and A8 atlas. The atlas staging buffer and device-local image are refreshed only after the atlas revision changes. An atlas dimension change invalidates UV normalization for retained geometry, so those buffers are regenerated once against the new dimensions.

## SPIR-V

The two shaders are checked into `shaders/` and embedded in `aurora.vulkan.shaders`. `tools/make_spirv.py` builds the modules directly from instruction words, removing a shader-compiler dependency from normal builds and making generated bytes reproducible.

The vertex shader passes clip-space position, UV, and color. The fragment shader samples red-channel coverage and multiplies it into vertex alpha.

## Synchronization and latency policy

Aurora allocates two reusable frame contexts. Each owns one command buffer, one image-acquired semaphore, and one submission fence. MAILBOX and IMMEDIATE presentation may use both contexts so command recording and GPU execution overlap. FIFO and FIFO-relaxed use only one context because those present modes are ordered and Aurora does not add a deeper application-side queue.

Render-finished semaphores are not owned by a frame context. Aurora creates one per swapchain image and signals the semaphore associated with the acquired image. Reacquiring that image establishes when the prior presentation operation using its semaphore has completed. This follows Khronos' swapchain-semaphore reuse guidance.

Retained geometry and the atlas image are shared across contexts. Transform-only frames only read those resources and can overlap. A content revision, atlas update, resize, or layer removal may rewrite/destroy them; before that rare mutation Aurora requires every frame fence to be idle.

Frame-context selection and `vkAcquireNextImageKHR` use zero-timeout readiness checks. If no context or image is ready, rendering is deferred rather than blocking input. The scene stores only current state, and its late-latch callback samples the captured pointer after acquisition and before command recording.

With `vsync = true` and `lowLatency = true`, Aurora requests MAILBOX and three images when supported, then FIFO-relaxed, then FIFO. With VSync disabled it requests IMMEDIATE, then MAILBOX, then FIFO. `AURORA_VSYNC` and `AURORA_LOW_LATENCY` override these options. See [Input-to-presentation latency](INPUT_LATENCY.md).

## Resize

A native resize updates the requested physical size and marks the swapchain dirty. Before the next frame Aurora waits for device idle, destroys swapchain-dependent resources, queries the surface, and rebuilds the swapchain, views, render pass, pipeline, and framebuffers. Retained layer content remains CPU-side and is uploaded against the new local physical dimensions as required.

`VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR` and `VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR` also mark the swapchain for recreation.

## Software retained composition

The software backend consumes the same base and layer draw lists. It caches:

- one opaque base ARGB surface by base revision;
- one transparent ARGB surface per retained layer by layer revision.

A transform-only frame copies the cached base and alpha-composites cached layers at their current device origins. It does not rerasterize those layers. The software path remains the deterministic screenshot/headless reference; Vulkan is the intended interactive path.

## Diagnostics

```d
RendererStats renderer = window.rendererStats();
writeln(renderer.frameDeferrals);
CompositorStats compositor = window.compositorStats();

writeln(renderer.frames);
writeln(renderer.geometryUploads);
writeln(renderer.geometryUploadBytes);
writeln(renderer.atlasUploads);
writeln(renderer.layerDraws);
writeln(compositor.transformOnlyFrames);
```

`resetRendererStats()` and `resetCompositorStats()` make focused interaction measurements possible.

## Validation layers

Set `options.vulkanValidation = true`. Aurora enables `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` only when the loader reports it; the layer is not a deployment dependency.

## macOS

AppKit creates and attaches a `CAMetalLayer` to the content view. Aurora requests `VK_EXT_metal_surface` and portability enumeration. A compatible loader such as MoltenVK must be installed separately. Automatic mode uses Core Graphics software presentation when a Vulkan loader is absent.

## Current performance boundaries

Implemented optimizations include retained per-layer GPU geometry, retained software surfaces, cached layer ordering, subpixel compositor transforms, late pointer latching, a frame-synchronized Win32 drag pointer, cached glyphs/layouts, batched clips, and mode-dependent frame overlap without stored drag states.

Remaining opportunities include partial atlas-region uploads, present-timing telemetry, analytic/instanced primitives, optional vendor latency extensions, a dedicated render thread, and device-loss recovery. Additional frame contexts must remain tied to replacement/non-ordered present modes rather than becoming an opaque FIFO latency queue.
